{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment is negative or shows strong bearish signals (e.g., -1.00 or 0.00 with recent declines).",
    "Increase forecast sensitivity to recent price spikes — if price rises sharply, model should not overshoot by more than 5% above recent peak.",
    "Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is consistently below true outcome over 5-7 days, gradually increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day toward historical mean.",
    "Reduce forecast volatility during low-sentiment periods — avoid large swings when sentiment is flat or negative.",
    "When sentiment is positive (e.g., 0.50 or above), allow slight upward bias but cap forecast at 10% above recent 7-day high to avoid overreaction.",
    "Correct for lag: if true outcome is rising while model is still reacting to prior data, add 0.3–0.5% per day to forecast to catch momentum.",
    "In high-sentiment periods, use sentiment as a multiplier: e.g., if sentiment = 0.50, increase forecast by 5–10% of the model’s baseline deviation."
  ]
}
